sections.heading: Optionality EIP Separation and EIP-8491 Status
sections.summary: The optionality problem has been factored out of Lucid into standalone EIP-8491, authored by Jannik; feedback still needed.
sections.body:
- The optionality problem has been isolated into a separate EIP (EIP-8491) rather than being folded into Lucid (EIP-8184), to reduce cognitive overhead in the already long and complex Lucid EIP.
- EIP-8491 received its number via [PR #12646](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12646/changes); it was previously referred to as EIPXXXX.
- Jannik confirmed the technical content is the same as previously proposed: a validator voting contract and the enforcement mechanism for key publisher priority lists. Additional rationale text was added.
- Justin Florentine provided only syntactical feedback so far; deeper review is still pending.
- The EIP may be easier to read for those already familiar with Lucid; newcomers may find the combined proposal in Lucid easier to follow.

sections.heading: CL Spec PR Status and Open Issues
sections.summary: The CL spec PR (consensus-specs #5403) needs further review; DOMAIN_SEALED_TRANSACTION_KEY_TIMELINESS and key publisher suffix values remain unresolved.
sections.body:
- The CL spec PR ([ethereum/consensus-specs#5403](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5403)) is not fully implemented; some items are still to-do pending ongoing encrypted mempool design decisions.
- Justin Traglia provided earlier feedback; Boma (Mercy) addressed those comments and responded to follow-up questions but needs further review from additional people.
- Boma flagged two specific open items requiring input from client teams or EIP authors:
  - `DOMAIN_SEALED_TRANSACTION_KEY_TIMELINESS` — the appropriate timeliness value is undetermined and needs a CL dev to weigh in.
  - Key publisher suffix — also unresolved.
- Justin Florentine acknowledged the team has been preoccupied with Glamsterdam and committed to finding CL-side reviewers.
- Boma offered to incorporate EIP-8491 changes (commitments, signature fields, validity checks) into the CL spec as a separate addition; Justin agreed this is fine as long as the changes remain separate from the Lucid spec.

sections.heading: Key Publisher Priority Lists and Optionality Abuse
sections.summary: Priority lists address probabilistic front-running but do not solve proposer optionality spam; governance acceptance remains uncertain.
sections.body:
- Gottfried raised concerns about the key publisher priority list approach:
  - It addresses probabilistic front-running (the main user-facing concern where users' funds can be stolen).
  - It does not address proposer optionality, where participants optimize latency to get transactions included regardless of list position — a more benign but still potentially spam-inducing form of optionality abuse.
- Governance and political feasibility are also a concern: multiple people have expressed skepticism about whether a validator-voting mechanism for key publisher priority will gain community acceptance.
- Gottfried acknowledged these are points to keep in mind rather than blocking issues.

sections.heading: Blind Sandwich Paper Assessment
sections.summary: The group found the blind sandwich paper's methodology questionable and its Ethereum findings negligible; consensus was to ignore it.
sections.body:
- A paper on blind sandwich attacks (shared previously in Telegram) was discussed. It covers multiple chains including Ethereum and Solana.
- Gottfried's main criticism: the paper lacks null hypothesis testing. It classifies sandwich attacks based on certain criteria but never establishes a baseline for what numbers would look like absent any malicious activity.
  - A legitimate arbitrage bot could randomly bracket honest transactions without exploiting privileged information, and the paper's methodology might flag these as attacks.
- The findings on Ethereum were described as "a bit of a nothing burger" — very little activity detected, likely because most users rely on private channels.
- Findings on other chains were described as "damning" with rampant sandwiching; the paper also covers Solana.
- Jannik noted the detected amounts were negligible and likely attributable to information leakage from MEV rebate protocols rather than fundamental protocol vulnerabilities.
- Justin Florentine suggested the paper could still serve as evidence of trust violations in supposedly private mempools, which could strengthen the case for encrypted mempools.
- Agreement: the paper should be largely ignored for purposes of this work.

sections.heading: Prototyping Readiness and Resource Constraints
sections.summary: No technical blockers to starting EL/CL prototypes, but no team members currently have capacity; work will proceed in the background.
sections.body:
- Justin Florentine proposed beginning EL and CL prototype implementations in parallel with ongoing spec review.
- No technical objections were raised; Jannik agreed it is possible to get started.
- Justin emphasized that prototyping is strategically valuable: the design phase is a first draft, and prototypes making "first contact with a devnet" will reveal aspects of Lucid and the optionality EIP that need to be revised or discarded.
- No one on the call had immediate capacity to begin prototyping:
  - Justin Florentine is focused on frames and has at least two higher priorities.
  - No other participants volunteered available bandwidth.
- The group acknowledged this as a constraint but not a blocker; prototyping will happen opportunistically in the background.

sections.heading: Shipping Timeline and Post-Quantum Implications
sections.summary: Encrypted mempools before I-Star is unrealistic; optimistic target is J-Star, with no schedule pressure warranted.
sections.body:
- Boma asked whether upcoming priorities (Hegota, post-quantum cryptography) would affect the encrypted mempool shipping timeline.
- Gottfried noted that post-quantum timelines are likely to accelerate significantly, requiring the community to "sprint" and sacrifice features along the way. Upcoming ACD calls are expected to be contentious on this topic.
- Agreement: getting encrypted mempools before I-Star is "completely unrealistic."
  - Justin Florentine added that I-Star itself may no longer be on the table; a realistic optimistic target is J-Star.
- These calls have been de-scoped to monthly cadence as a touchpoint. No schedule pressure is warranted for encrypted mempool work.
- Next meeting in one month; prototypes may or may not be ready to discuss.
